articles.title: Gay adult entertainers share their shocking & emotional coming-out stories
articles.description: Grab the tissues for the latest episode of Crush House. The sexy new reality show stars a cast of notable gay adult entertainers who are competing to be crowned the show's "Most Valuable Crush." Hosted by adult film superstars Josh Moore and JJ Aussie, ten adult creators from all over the world are not only going head-to-head in steamy challenges, but they're also opening up on the hardships that have come with their careers. In the season's most vulnerable and personal episode yet, the seven remaining contestants — Beau Butler, Austin Ponce, Horse Papo, Huge Ajax, Roxas Caelum, Tim James, Victor Vivone — confide in one another on the struggles as queer creators in the adult industry. Although they've achieved great success, their very public careers have strained relationships with their loved ones over the years. The raw and heartfelt exchanges from the Crushes go as deep as family members not accepting them and even honoring the anniversary of the recent passing of a loved one. Set in a luxurious Baja California villa , the reality series explores attraction, relationships, identity, friendship and contemporary queer life. In upcoming episodes, the Crushes left will navigate strategies, alliances and eliminations. They will also dig into honest, emotional conversations about their experiences as content creators and the challenges they face both personally and professionally. With the finale slated to air November 20 on MenCrush, two winners will be announced: one chosen by the Crushes and a second chosen by the audience through weekly voting on MenCrush.com. The show's "Most Valuable Crush" will win a personalized documentary by MenCrush and a cash prize of $20,000 sponsored by MISTR. Check out some of the vulnerable responses below and the trailer below. Watch the full episode of Crush House on the official website here. Tim James Tim James is a popular adult entertainer who's also gone viral as a content creator across platforms. His token phrase "verse bottom body builder" has helped him create a consistent brand. In the new episode, he opened up on his difficult coming-out journey with his father at a young age. "I was raised extremely Catholic. When I came out, the first thing my dad said was, 'You may as well have told me you have cancer.' He would call me crying saying, 'Are you sure you're gay?' I was really depressed and gained 25 pounds in six weeks. Now that I look back on it, he loved me so much and literally thought I would get AIDS and die. When I had that realization, I was able to let go of the shame of being gay." Victor Vivone Hailing from Brazil, Victor Vivone is bringing a unique perspective on navigating fame as he competes to become the first MVC. Although his career is taking off in the adult entertainment industry, he's sadly on the outs with his family. "Unfortunately, I don't have a relationship with my family right now. They've never understood what I do. It was so hard to come out as a gay guy. They never really accepted me for who I am. You want to do what makes you happy, but you want love from people who have the same blood as you." The relationship became increasingly toxic as Vivone got older, even resulting in physical abuse. Horse Papo Horse Papo has become quite a recognizable face in the adult entertainment industry, but he thankfully has a strong relationship with his blood family. "I'm the closest with my parents. All they want for me is to be happy and leave a good, positive footprint. I don't tell them every single detail, but they have an idea of what I do. They see that I have a good head on my shoulders and that's what they're most proud of. They're most proud of the man I've become today." Roxas Caelum WIth only a few years under his belt in the adult entertainment industry, Roxas Caelum has built a strong relationship with his family. "I came out as bisexual in high school and my parents didn't care one bit. My mom doesn't accept what I do, but she's okay with it. She's proud with how successful in life I am. My dad doesn't really care too much. My family is more open than conservative. I have a great relationship with my whole family."

articles.title: Taika Waititi’s Star Wars film is the latest to hit the buffers. At some point Lucasfilm is going to have to actually make a movie
articles.description: Waititi joins a long list of movie-makers who were expected to bring a new direction to the franchise, before the studio appeared to get cold feet Movie-making these days is a very expensive endeavour. In 1977, George Lucas’s Star Wars cost $11m to make, which would be approximately $60m in today’s money, and has since amassed $775m at the global box office, including rereleases. Fast forward to 2026 and the most recent film in the long-running space saga, The Mandalorian and Grogu, cost a reported $165m and brought in $346m worldwide. If there was ever a Hollywood gold rush, the mines ran dry long ago. Perhaps this is one of the reasons why Disney-owned Lucasfilm seems to be so terrified of making new Star Wars movies. Since 2019’s The Rise of Skywalker, only one Star Wars film, the aforementioned Mando and Grogu movie, has actually made it into cinemas. But that has not stopped the studio announcing a small armada of other projects – sometimes via press release, more often at various high-profile celebrations, conferences or other corporate jamborees – that have so far failed to reach multiplexes.
